subject.title: Reply-session init conflict is silently dropped on Slack/webchat/heartbeat inbound, though Telegram already treats it as retryable

question: Should this issue be closed only after the shared reply-session-init self-heal is proven to cover transient distinct-message drops, or should maintainers require explicit WebChat/heartbeat/Discord retry parity in addition to that PR?
rationale: Current source shows both the central CAS throw and surface-specific terminalization paths, while the latest live comment argues the open shared PR covers a related permanent wedge but not necessarily this transient drop mode.

options.title: Review Shared Fix Then Prove Parity
options.body: Land or reject the shared self-heal first, then keep this issue open until WebChat/heartbeat/Discord transient-drop proof shows the reported messages are preserved or retried.

options.title: Require Surface Retry Now
options.body: Treat explicit WebChat/heartbeat/Discord retry or coalescing as required work independent of the shared self-heal PR.

options.title: Defer Until More Live Proof
options.body: Ask for a focused current-main live reproduction that isolates WebChat or heartbeat before choosing the owner boundary.

recommendation.title: Review Shared Fix Then Prove Parity
recommendation.body: Land or reject the shared self-heal first, then keep this issue open until WebChat/heartbeat/Discord transient-drop proof shows the reported messages are preserved or retried.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent session-accessor and gateway chat work makes jalehman the best available owner for the shared-vs-surface fix boundary decision.
